title: Terraform module: key-provider shim with Vault connector and Secrets reconciler
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reusable Terraform module that implements a lightweight key-provider shim and secrets reconciler to enable customers to route encryption operations to cloud KMS or on-prem HSMs while synchronizing application secrets with either HashiCorp Vault or cloud Secrets Manager. The module should be opinionated about configuration surfaces (provider blocks, key aliasing, rotation policies) but flexible enough to support PKCS#11 HSMs, cloud KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure), and Vault KV v2. It must include health checks, automated upgrade paths for key material, and a plan for rolling secret re-encryption during module upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes a stable interface: variables for provider_type, kms_key_alias, hsm_pkcs11_config, vault_address, secrets_manager_type, and reconcile_interval
Implements a provider abstraction layer so callers can choose 'cloud-kms', 'hsm-pkcs11', or 'vault-native' with the same module outputs
Includes automated smoke health checks that verify: key lookup, sign/encrypt roundtrip, and secret read/write to configured secret backend
Provides a documented migration path for key rotation that avoids double-encryption and supports zero-downtime rolling re-encrypt for services
Module creates Terraform outputs required by private deployment bootstrap (key_arn_or_slot, secret_backend_endpoint, reconciler_service_account)
Comprehensive unit/integration tests run in CI using the terraform-test harness and a Vault dev server or cloud KMS emulator
design_decisions: Abstraction: implement a 'key_provider' interface in the module instead of separate modules per backend to reduce duplication
HSM support: use PKCS#11 configuration template and document required network routing and certs; do not bake vendor drivers into module
Secrets sync: reconciler will be a small controller (daemon) deployed as a systemd unit or k8s Job depending on customer deployment; Terraform will provide configuration and service identity only
Rotation policy: prefer staged key material approach (create new key version, rewrap secrets with new key, then deprecate old key) to allow rollback
Health checks: implement both Terraform provisioned 'smoke' checks (null_resource + local-exec) and runtime probes surfaced to Redwood Console metrics
implementation_notes: Module code layout: /modules/key-provider-shim/{main.tf,variables.tf,outputs.tf,README.md,examples} with subfolders for providers (aws/, gcp/, azure/, pkcs11/)
Use provider-specific helper modules for low-level resources (aws_kms_alias, google_kms_crypto_key, azure_key_vault_key) and keep top-level module agnostic
Expose a 'reconcile_bootstrap' boolean to optionally deploy a minimal Vault token/secret engine configuration via Terraform for small customers
Do not attempt to manage customer data plane VMs; only manage identities, policy bindings, and bootstrapping resources
Make secrets reconciler idempotent and safe for re-run; store reconciler state in Vault or DynamoDB depending on deployment
test_plan: Unit tests for Terraform using terratest: validate variable permutations and output shapes
Integration: pipeline job that spins up a VPC test environment with a dev Vault server and AWS KMS emulator, executes reconciler smoke tests
Chaos test: simulate KMS failover and verify module's fallback behavior and reconciler backoff metrics
Upgrade test: exercise key rotation sequence and confirm no secret is lost and services can fetch re-encrypted secrets during rollout
